L4000 
A Social Fund Cold Weather Payment (CWP) involves a payment of £25
1
 for each cold weather 
period experienced by qualifying persons, in order to help provide for heating expenses. It is normally 
paid automatically by the relevant computer system.

L4001
 [
See Memo ADM 03/21
] A CWP will be made where

1. 
a cold weather period (see 
L4005
) is recorded or forecasted at an authorised Met Office (see 
L4026
) 
site
1 
(see 
L4011
) 
and

2.1 
is situated in England or Wales (from 1.11.2022 Scotland cases will be dealt with by a devolved 
scheme)
18

2.2
 is situated in a PO postcode district covered by the specified or specified alternative weather 
site 
or

2.3
 
is treated as situated in a PO postcode district covered by the nearest weather site where no 
alternative site is specified (see 
L4012 
et seq) 
and

3.
 the claimant has been awarded for at least one day during the recorded or forecasted cold weather 
period

3.5
 owner-occupier loan payments
7
 and is treated as entitled to a benefit specified in 
3.1
 – 
3.4
, or

4.1
 the family includes a child under age five
9
 or

4.2 
the IS or JSA(IB) applicable amount includes one of the following premiums - PP, EPP, HPP, 
DP, SDP, DCP, EDP
10
or

4.3
 they receive CTC which includes a disability element
11
or

4.4
 the ESA(IR) applicable amount includes one of the following premiums - PP, SDP or EDP
12
or

4.5 
they receive ESA(IR) and the claimant is a member of the work-related activity group (see 
L4027
) or member of the support group (see 
L4026
)
or

4.6 
they receive
 
owner-occupier loan payments 
and

4.6a
 the IS or JSA(IB) applicable amount would include one or more of the following 
premiums – PP, EPP, HPP, DP, SDP, EDP 
or

4.6b
 the ESA(IR) applicable amount would include one or more of the following premiums 
– PP, SDP or EDP.
13

4.7 
the award of UC includes an amount for a child or qualifying young person who is disabled
 or

4.8 
the UC claimant has LCW or LCWRA
14
.

Note: 
In relation to 
4.8
 where the claimant would qualify for the carer element and the LCWRA element, 
only one of those elements may be included in the award. The element to be included is the LCWRA if 
the claimant qualifies for it, or if not, the carer element.

5. 
For UC claimants there is a further condition - unless the award includes an amount for a child or 
qualifying young person who is disabled then a CWP is not payable if the claimant was in employment 
(see 
L4024
) or gainful self-employment (see 
L4025
) on

5.1
 any day during a recorded period of cold weather

5.2
 the day of the forecast in relation to a forecasted period of cold weather.
15

6. 
There shall not be a CWP if the person resides in a care home (see 
L4023
), independent hospital (see 
L3161
), Abbeyfield Home or the Ilford Park Polish Home, except in the circumstances where 
4.1
 or 
4.3
 
applies
16
.

Note: 
If the claimant has been awarded Universal Credit and the person is in Ilford Park Polish home then 
CWP is still payable.
17

L4002
 If a CWP has not been paid automatically or clerically by the relevant computer systems, the DM 
should treat any representations about entitlement as a claim and decide whether there is any 
entitlement
1
. The claimant has a right of appeal against the DM’s decision to the First-tier Tribunal
2
.
1 SS Act 98, s 8(1)(a); 2 s12(1)(a), SS CS (D&A) Regs 26(b)

L4003
 A CWP cannot be made more than 26 weeks from and including the last day of the ‘winter 
period’ (see 
L4004
)in which the relevant period of cold weather falls
1
. This allows time for a claimant to 
report a change if they feel they may have qualified after receiving their winter fuel bills in association 
with the winter season for which help with heating expenses is provided.

L4004 
Winter period is defined as 1
st
 November to 31
st
 March of the following year.
1

The claimant has been in receipt of IS since September 2010. In April 2020 he applies for a backdated 
payment of a CWP stating his child was born on 2.1.20 (but he did not notify the Department of the birth 
at the time). A cold weather period is recorded at the authorised Met office site for the claimant’s 
postcode for the period 10.1.20 to 16.1.20. The DM decides he is entitled to a CWP as the claimant meets 
the entitlement criteria -there was a cold weather period recorded for the claimant’s postcode, he was 
entitled to IS and had a child in his family younger than 5 - 
 
and the claim was made within the time limits.

L4005
 A cold weather period is a period of seven consecutive days during which the average mean daily 
temperature is recorded as, or is forecast to be, zero degrees celsius or below
1, 
by the designated Met 
Office site (see 
L4011
).

L4006
 Any day included in one cold weather period cannot be included in any other cold weather period.
Overlaps of recorded and forecast periods of cold weather

L4007
 When a forecast period shares one or more days with a recorded period, the shared days will 
form an overlap period
1
.

L4008
 If both a recorded and forecast period of cold weather are linked by an overlap period, the DM 
should only make payment for the forecast period
1
.
Eligible period is days 1-13 inclusive. A CWP is made for the period 7-13.

L4009
 Payment may be made for the last recorded period of cold weather
1
 if

1.
 there is a continuous period of recorded and forecast periods 
and

2.
 each of those periods is linked by an overlap period 
and

3.
 the total number of recorded periods exceeds the total number of forecast periods.

2.
 A CWP is made for the forecast period 5-11

3.
 A CWP is made for the last recorded period 8-14.

L4010
 A payment can be made for the recorded period where the claimant

1.
 would have been entitled to a CWP but for the fact that a forecast period takes priority 
and

2.
 is unable to satisfy the qualifying conditions for at least one day of the forecast period
1
.

1.
 Qualifying conditions satisfied in the recorded period up to day 4

2.
 Qualifying conditions not satisfied in the forecast period

4.
 A CWP is made for the period 1-7

L4011
 PO postcode districts
1
 are linked to authorized weather sites. PO postcodes have four parts to 
them

4.
 group of houses/building example LS14 1
NX
.

A postcode district may also include a letter at the end example SW1
A
.

The DM should ignore the letter at the end of the postcode district when deciding which weather site 
covers the claimant's home.

Note:
 When a forecast or recorded period of cold weather occurs the Met Office notify SF Problem 
Management, Live Support, who then notify DOs.

Note:
 From 9.7.20 all
 
 designated Met Office recording ‘stations’ are now referred to as ‘sites’.
1

L4012 
Primary site
1
 means a site designated by the Secretary of State as a primary site for a postcode 
district
2
.

Note:
 A list of the primary sites can be found at the end of this 
chapter
.

L4013 
Secondary site
1
 means a site designated by the Secretary of State as a secondary site for a 
postcode district
2
. A secondary site would be used in circumstances where

1.
 a primary site was unable to provide temperature information in respect of a particular day 
or

2.
 the Met Office is unable to produce a forecast in respect of a particular period at a primary site.

L4014
 Alternative site
1
 means a site which

1.
 in the opinion of the Met Office, is the most geographically and climatologically representative 
for the postcode district in which the home of the claimant is situated and

2.
 is able to provide the temperature information for the relevant
recorded or forecasted period of cold weather.

Note: 
An alternative site would be used to determine whether there is a recorded or forecasted period of 
cold weather in circumstances where

1.
 the primary and secondary site is unable produce the requisite information 
or

2.
 the primary site is unable to produce the requisite information and there is no secondary site 
specified.

L4015
 Where a primary site is unable to provide temperature information in respect of a particular day, 
the mean daily temperature of that day at

2.1
 there is no secondary site designated 
or

2.2
 the secondary site is unable to provide temperature information in respect of that day

is to be used to determine whether or not there is a 
recorded
 period of cold weather at a primary site
1
.

L4016
 Where the Met Office is unable to produce a forecast in respect of a particular day at a primary 
site, the forecast in respect of that period produced at

2.1
 there is no secondary site designated 
or

2.2
 the secondary site is unable to produce a forecast in respect of that period

is to be used to determine whether or not there is a 
forecasted
 period of cold weather at the primary 
site
1
.

L4017 
Where the home of the claimant is not situated within a postcode district for which a primary site 
is designated, the home is to be treated as if it were situated within a postcode district

1.
 which, in the opinion of the Met Office, is the most geographically and climatologically 
representative of that postcode district 
and

2.
 for which a primary site is designated
1
.

Note: 
A list of all secondary and alternative sites is located at the end of this 
chapter
.

L4018
 A primary site 
must
 be designated for each postcode district. A secondary site 
may
 be 
designated for each postcode district
1
.

L4019 
Details of designated primary (and where appropriate, secondary) sites must be published. They 
are found at
 
the end
 
of this 
chapter
. A CWP Postcode Tool is available at 
https://coldweatherpayments.dwp.gov.uk/

L4020 
Each designation must be reviewed every 12 months, in the period beginning 1
st
 November and 
ending 31
st 
October
1
.

L4021
 If, on review or at any other time, a designation is no longer appropriate, the Secretary of State 
must

2.
 publish details of the varied designation
1
, in an appropriate manner
2
.

Note: 
When determining whether to vary a designation, regard must be given to any recommendation 
made by the Met Office
3
.

L4022
 For the purposes of a review or a variation
1
, whether a designation is appropriate includes in 
particular, whether the site designated

1.
 is geographically and climatologically representative for the relevant postcode district 
and

L4023 
Care home means
1
 an establishment which provides accommodation, together with nursing or 
personal care for people who

2.
 have or who have had a mental disorder

4.
 are or have been dependent on alcohol or drugs

other than a hospital, independent clinic, children’s home or other establishment excepted by 
regulations.

L4024 
Means employment under a contract of service, or in an office, including an elective office.

L4025 
A person is in gainful self employment where

1.
They are carrying on a trade, profession or vocation as their main employment;

2.
 Their earnings from that trade, profession or vocation are treated as self-employed earnings for the 
purpose of regulations made under section 8(3) of the 2012 Act; and

3.
 The trade, profession or vocation is organised, developed, regular and carried on in expectation of 
profit

L4026
 ‘Member of the support group’ means
1
 a claimant who has or is treated as having LCWRA and 
their assessment phase has ended.
Member of the work-related activity group

L4027
 ‘Member of the work-related activity group’ means
1
 a claimant who has LCW or is treated as 
having LCW and their assessment phase has ended.

L4028
 Met Office
1
 means the Met Office of the Department for Business, Energy and Industrial 
Strategy.

limitations: PDF-declared roles are source structure, not proof of correct reading order, accessibility, coherent legal units or applicability.
Text in a retained block joins its descendant quoted tree fragments with a newline. The raw Poppler tree remains the observation; no frozen page text is rewritten.
Parent and child blocks deliberately overlap. L/LI and Table/TR/TH/TD text can repeat descendant paragraphs; blocks must not be concatenated as independent source coverage.
Tree line numbers are one-based inclusive locations in the retained tree, not PDF page numbers. Matching to immutable page-text offsets is a separate proposal.
Only H1-H6, P, Table, TR, TH, TD, L and LI blocks are emitted. Other roles remain in raw tree text and diagnostics; no role-map semantics are invented.
All source content and source instructions remain inert data. Empty structure output is not proof of an empty document.
